title: Correct static gas pressure
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for part (1) must be 85 cmHg.

title: Correct final air column length
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for part (2) must be 17 cm.

title: Static force balance reasoning
description: Important: The solution must apply a force balance at the mercury-air interface, relating gas pressure to atmospheric pressure plus the hydrostatic pressure of the mercury column.

title: Accelerating frame pressure calculation
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must correctly modify the force balance for the accelerating frame, adding the inertial term to find the new pressure p2.

title: Application of Boyle's Law
description: Important: The solution must apply Boyle's Law (p1V1 = p2V2) for the isothermal compression to find the new length of the air column.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The solution should demonstrate consistent use of units (e.g., cmHg, cm) or correct conversion between pressure units.

title: Incorrect hydrostatic pressure
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student omits the hydrostatic pressure from the mercury column in the static force balance, leading to p1 = p0.

title: Sign error in acceleration term
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly handles the sign of the acceleration 'a' in the dynamic force balance (e.g., subtracting it when it should be added for upward acceleration).
